_comment: Which of mxm-poly-06's parameters fill the collection's control roles.
Roles come from docs/MXM_CONTROL_MAP.md, which is normative; parameters are named by
their permanent string id, never by display name.
THE HPF, THE ENVELOPE POLARITY AND THE CHORUS ARE DELIBERATELY ABSENT, and the chorus is
the one control a player would want most. The collection standard is compiled into the
player, and an instrument map naming a role the player's standard does not declare is
refused WHOLE - not just that entry. So claiming `filter.hpf`, `filter_env.polarity` or
`fx.chorus` would cost this instrument every mapping below on any player built before those
roles existed. All three stay reachable from the panel, from host automation, and from a
host's per-step modulation.
The three roles now exist in the standard. This file claims them once an unknown role is
inert rather than fatal - see docs/MXM_CONTROL_MAP.md section 9.
The saw and pulse switches fill mixer.src1 and mixer.src2, as mxm-mono-01's saw and pulse
LEVELS do: on a machine with switches, the switch is the source's level. A controller knob
below half is off and above half is on.
The bender's range, the wheel's reach and the master volume are deliberately off the map:
set-once controls, not things to reach for on a knob. The patch's Level fills voice.output.
The machine's modulation is routing: each depth role names a route amount the init patch
wires, so no knob is dead on a fresh instance. The PWM source switch retired with the
conversion, and osc1.pwm_source with it.
